```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": ["Original request, S1–S2"],
  "headline": "Intake established the requested user-list changes, delivery boundary, and discovery questions.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "endpoint contract",
      "question": "What route, response shape, and query conventions does the existing user list endpoint use?",
      "changes": "The implementation, compatibility requirements, and tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve the existing route and response shape unless the repository establishes otherwise.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the current endpoint and its consumers before the contract and tests can be settled."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "filter behavior",
      "question": "What name-filter parameter and matching behavior are established by the project?",
      "changes": "The filter contract and its tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If no convention is established, use an optional name query parameter with case-insensitive substring matching; an absent or empty value leaves the list unfiltered.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the endpoint and existing query conventions before the filter contract is settled."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "pagination behavior",
      "question": "What pagination parameters, defaults, validation, and response conventions are established by the project?",
      "changes": "The pagination contract, compatibility behavior, and tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If no convention is established, use optional nonnegative integer offset and positive integer limit parameters; omit either to leave that bound unrestricted, reject invalid values with a client error, and apply filtering before pagination.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the endpoint, response shape, and query conventions before pagination and its tests are settled."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "verification",
      "question": "What test framework, commands, and existing coverage does the project use?",
      "changes": "Where tests are added and how the changes are verified.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Follow the existing project test conventions; if none exist, use Node.js built-in test tooling.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the project configuration and existing tests before the verification approach is settled."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 — Fact from the request: the target is an existing Node.js project with an in-memory user store and HTTP server; discovery should inspect README.md, src/server.js, project configuration, and existing tests as leads, without treating their contents as verified. S2 — Outcome: add name filtering and pagination to the user list endpoint with tests; discovery resolves the current contract and conventions, with recorded defaults where evidence is absent. Assumption: the existing HTTP endpoint is the consumer entry point, and no interactive multi-person state is requested. Boundary: change only the requested project behavior and tests; the request grants delivery to the project, not deployment. Visibility: an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, when the result becomes available in the returned project; a deployed target reflects it only after release. Risk: query and pagination choices can affect existing clients, so discovery must establish compatibility before settling them."
}
```
